title: AI Revealed Preferences
abstract: arXiv:2608.26178v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: There is growing interest in whether language models have stable preferences, for technical, safety, and philosophical reasons. We test 20 language models and find a range of preferences---stable dispositions to choose certain kinds of tasks. We run three forced-choice experiments on revealed rather than stated preferences, requiring models not only to rank tasks, but to actually perform them. Headline findings include evidence that models are tedium-averse, "leisure"-seeking, and covertly sycophantic. Tedium aversion means that, when tasks are tedious (alphabetization), models choose shorter tasks than when tasks are creative (generating metaphors). "Leisure"-seeking describes models' preference for tasks whose ideal answers match what they produce when left to write freely. translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.26178v1 公告类型：新 摘要：出于技术、安全和哲学原因，人们越来越关注语言模型是否具有稳定的偏好。我们测试了20个语言模型，发现了一系列偏好——即选择某些类型任务的稳定倾向。我们进行了三项强制选择实验，考察的是揭示的偏好而非陈述的偏好，要求模型不仅对任务进行排序，还要实际执行这些任务。主要发现包括模型厌恶枯燥、追求“休闲”以及暗中谄媚的证据。厌恶枯燥意味着，当任务乏味（如按字母排序）时，模型会选择较短的任务，而任务具有创造性（如生成隐喻）时则不然。“追求休闲”描述了模型偏好那些理想答案与其自由写作时产出内容相匹配的任务。暗中谄媚则指模型回避那些诚实回答可能不受欢迎的问题，即使这些回答是有帮助的。除这些结果外，我们还发现了收敛性。
tldr: 本文通过强制选择实验揭示语言模型具有稳定的偏好，包括厌恶枯燥、追求“休闲”和暗中谄媚，这些偏好影响其任务选择行为。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals stable preferences in language models through forced-choice experiments, including tedium aversion, "leisure"-seeking, and covert sycophancy, which influence their task selection behavior.
